Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, yes... she has astigmatism, which means her eyes don't focus properly on things. It's been a challenge for her, especially when trying to read or watch TV. We're really worried about how this might affect her learning.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: She had fluid in her ear for a while, and we were so scared it would affect her hearing permanently. Luckily, after treatment, everything seems back to normal now. But I still get anxious whenever she complains about her ear.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Chewing has been an issue for her since she started eating solid foods. Some foods are just too hard for her to manage. We've had to adjust her diet accordingly to make sure she can eat comfortably.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: The cardiologist says she needs regular check-ups to monitor her heart health. I try to stay on top of these appointments because I know how crucial they are for her well-being. It's always a relief when the results come back normal.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Developmentally, she's been slower than her peers to reach certain milestones like walking or sitting. It was worrying at first, but with therapy and support, she's making progress. I'm just eager for her to catch up.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Food textures can be a real issue for her. She's very picky and will only eat certain things if they're prepared in specific ways. Mealtime can be challenging, but we're learning to navigate her preferences.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Yes... two main concerns. Firstly, her fontanelle took longer than usual to close completely. And secondly, her speech development isn't where it should be for her age. She doesn't speak as much as other children her age. Both these things worry me and I hope we can find ways to support her better.
report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient:
- Astigmatism affecting reading and watching TV
- Fluid buildup in the ear requiring treatment
- Difficulty chewing food due to tooth issues

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Many children have fluid buildup in the ear requiring treatment
- Some have difficulty chewing food due to tooth issues

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- Need for regular heart checks due to potential heart conditions
- One study found 11% of children with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which requires MRI review

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Many children with KBG syndrome have heart conditions
- Some have tethered cord, which requires MRI review

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- Feeding difficulties leading to dietary adjustments
- Challenging mealtime experiences due to food texture restrictions

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Some children have difficulty chewing food due to tooth issues

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- Slower than peers in reaching developmental milestones
- Speech delays

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Many children with KBG syndrome show developmental delays and speech delays

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
- Fontanelle taking longer than usual to close
- Challenges with speech development

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Some children have challenges with speech development

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
- Astigmatism affecting vision
- Need for regular eye exams

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Many children with KBG syndrome have vision concerns

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
- Difficulty chewing food due to tooth issues

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Some children have difficulty chewing food due to tooth issues

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
- Needs additional help in school
- May require special schooling or remain in mainstream with EHCP

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though some go to mainstream primary schools

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
- Worrying developmental delays and speech delays
- Concerns around cognitive abilities and behavioral differences

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Many children with KBG syndrome exhibit behavioral differences and developmental delays

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
- Brachydactyly and clinodactyly of the fingers
- Possible curvature of the 5th finger
- Spinal abnormalities, including possible scoliosis

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Some children with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including possible scoliosis

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
- Regular dental check-ups
- Regular hearing reviews to age 5
- Ophthalmology review
- Cardiac review following diagnosis
- Skeletal review (wrist X-ray, hip, spine, and skull X-rays)
- Palate review (if concerns around feeding or speech persist)
- Consider review and investigation for tethered cord (MRI) where clinical concerns arise on an individual basis
- Monitor growth velocity: if height is below the 2nd centile, consider referral for endocrine investigations
- Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy
- Dietary modifications based on feeding difficulties and food texture restrictions

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our daughter has hypermetropia, which means she has a higher-than-normal curvature of her cornea. This affects how she sees objects at different distances. She sometimes struggles with focusing, especially when looking at things close-up. 

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes, our child had fluid buildup in her ears a couple of times. It affected her ability to hear clearly and caused discomfort. Thankfully, after treatment‚ it cleared up‚ but we monitor her ears regularly now.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Her teeth seem prone to chipping or breaking easier than they should. Even minor accidents can cause noticeable damage‚ so we have to ensure she’s extra careful during meals and playtime to avoid any incidents.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Compared to other kids‚ she tires out faster during physical activities. While she can run around and have fun‚ we notice she needs breaks sooner than her friends do. It might be related to her overall energy levels rather than a specific heart condition‚ but we keep an eye on it.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves‚ muscle tone‚ fits).
Parent: Unfortunately‚ she falls more frequently than other children her age. Whether it’s due to coordination or balance issues‚ we’re working with her to improve strength and agility to reduce these incidents.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding‚ stomach‚ bowel).
Parent: Feeding has been challenging for her since infancy. Certain textures and tastes make mealtime difficult‚ and she has sensitivities to particular foods that trigger digestive discomfort.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Besides the mentioned issues‚ our child moves slightly differently compared to her peers. There’s also a concern regarding delayed fontanelle closure‚ where certain bones in her skull took longer to fully close than typically expected. These aspects require periodic assessments to monitor progress and adjust care accordingly.
report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our daughter experiences occasional respiratory infections, particularly during cold seasons. These episodes tend to resolve quickly with standard pediatric interventions.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Respiratory infections are relatively common in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the presence of enlarged tonsils and adenoids, which can contribute to airway obstruction and frequent viral infections.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our daughter requires routine echocardiograms to monitor for potential cardiovascular issues, including valve abnormalities and structural heart defects. These scans have shown no significant concerns thus far.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Individuals with KBG syndrome are predisposed to congenital heart defects, including valve abnormalities and structural heart conditions. Regular cardiac evaluations are crucial for early detection and intervention.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our daughter exhibits feeding difficulties, characterized by selective eating habits and sensitivity to certain textures and flavors. These challenges impact her nutritional intake and overall growth.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Gastrointestinal issues, such as food intolerances and selective eating patterns, are commonly observed in individuals with KBG syndrome. Management strategies, including dietary modifications and behavioral therapies, are essential for improving digestion and nutrition.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our daughter has experienced recurrent otitis media and temporary hearing loss, necessitating repeat grommet insertions and consideration of hearing aid usage.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Recurrent ear infections, including otitis media and glue ear, are frequent complications in individuals with KBG syndrome. Early intervention, such as timely grommet insertion and hearing aid fitting, is critical for managing these issues effectively.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our daughter displays a tendency towards falls and injuries, possibly due to unsteady gait and coordination deficits. Physical therapy and adaptive equipment have helped mitigate these risks.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Neurological manifestations, such as reduced muscle tone and coordination, are typical in individuals with KBG syndrome. Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and assistive devices are vital components of management plans.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
Our daughter has experienced recurrent otitis media and temporary hearing loss, requiring repeat grommet insertions and consideration of hearing aid usage.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Ear infections, including otitis media and glue ear, are common complications in individuals with KBG syndrome. Early intervention, such as timely grommet insertion and hearing aid fitting, is critical for managing these issues effectively.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
Our daughter has experienced vision-related issues, such as astigmatism and short-sightedness (myopia), affecting her ability to focus on distant objects. Regular eye examinations are recommended to monitor progression and address any refractive errors promptly.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Vision problems, including astigmatism and short-sightedness, are frequently encountered in individuals with KBG syndrome. Ophthalmological evaluations, including comprehensive eye checks and corrective lenses, are essential for maintaining optimal visual function.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our daughter shows no notable skin concerns beyond the typical variations seen in children with KBG syndrome. Routine dermatological assessments are advised to monitor for any emerging issues.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Skin characteristics, such as eczema and acne, are common among individuals with KBG syndrome. Regular dermatological evaluations are crucial for identifying and managing any unique skin concerns.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
Our daughter faces challenges with tooth decay and chipping, exacerbated by her propensity for accidental bites. Enhanced dental hygiene practices and the use of fluoride varnish are recommended to promote better oral health.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Tooth decay and chipping are frequent occurrences in individuals with KBG syndrome. Implementing stricter dental protocols, such as enhanced brushing techniques and fluoride applications, is essential for preventing these issues.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
Our daughter benefits from additional educational support, including specialized programs tailored to her cognitive and behavioral needs. Transitioning to secondary school presents unique challenges, requiring ongoing adaptation and accommodations.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Educational requirements vary widely depending on the severity of developmental delays and behavioral differences. Tailored educational approaches, including individualized education plans (IEPs) and resource rooms, are crucial for supporting students with KBG syndrome throughout their academic careers.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
Our daughter exhibits behavioral traits consistent with the broader KBG syndrome phenotype, including heightened sensitivity to stimuli and social interactions. Behavioral therapy and targeted interventions are integral to her holistic development.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Behavioral profiles, encompassing sensitivity to stimuli, social interaction challenges, and executive function impairments, are universal hallmarks of KBG syndrome. Evidence-based behavioral therapies and supportive environments are pivotal for fostering emotional regulation and social competence.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
Our daughter demonstrates brachydactyly, characterized by shortened fingers, and clinodactyly, involving inward-curving of the fifth finger. These skeletal features contribute to her overall physical profile.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Skeletal anomalies, such as brachydactyly and clinodactyly, are prevalent in individuals with KBG syndrome. Orthodontic interventions, splints, and orthopedic surgeries may be considered for enhancing limb alignment and functionality.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Problems with vision or eyes:
Recommendations: Regular ophthalmological check-ups starting from infancy to monitor for any changes in vision or eye health. Address any refractive errors promptly with suitable corrective measures.

b) Problems with heart:
Recommendations: Continue regular cardiac evaluations post-diagnosis to monitor for any evolving heart conditions. Follow medical advice regarding medication and lifestyle adjustments as per cardiologist guidance.

c) Problems with gastrointestinal system:
Recommendations: Maintain a balanced diet rich in fiber and nutrients to support overall digestive health. Encourage a varied diet to prevent food intolerances and allergies. Consult a gastroenterologist for personalized dietary and therapeutic recommendations.

d) Problems with neurological system:
Recommendations: Engage in regular neurodevelopmental assessments to track progress and identify any areas needing further support. Collaborate with neurologists and specialists to develop a comprehensive rehabilitation plan.

e) Problems with immune system:
Recommendations: Monitor immunoglobulin levels and vaccine reactions closely. Discuss with pediatricians the necessity and timing of vaccinations based on individual risk factors and medical history.

f) Problems with kidney:
Recommendations: Perform annual renal ultrasounds and urine analyses to detect any underlying kidney issues. Follow nephrology guidelines for managing kidney-related concerns.

g) Problems with thyroid:

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences occasional respiratory infections and requires vaccinations against pneumococcus and Haemophilus influenzae type b.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Respiratory infections are common in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the presence of a functional variant in the ANKRD11 gene, which impairs the production of functional proteins involved in immune cell function.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a history of congenital heart defects, specifically a valve anomaly requiring periodic follow-up visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Cardiovascular anomalies are frequent in KBG syndrome, including structural abnormalities of the heart valves and potential patent ductus arteriosus, which can lead to persistent circulation between the pulmonary artery and the aorta. Regular cardiovascular assessments are crucial to monitor for complications and ensure timely interventions.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits feeding difficulties and slow weight gain, which are consistent with the gastrointestinal concerns associated with KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome commonly experience delays in reaching developmental milestones related to feeding and digestion, along with a tendency towards gastroesophageal reflux disease and delayed gastric emptying. Management strategies focusing on dietary modifications and therapeutic options tailored to the patient's specific needs are essential.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a compromised immune system, increasing susceptibility to infections and necessitating vaccinations against Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae type b.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: The immunodeficiency aspect of KBG syndrome contributes to frequent opportunistic infections, highlighting the importance of prophylactic measures and ongoing surveillance for infectious diseases.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient demonstrates coordination challenges, particularly evident during physical activities, which reflects the neuromotor impairments commonly observed in KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Neurodevelopmental outcomes in KBG syndrome encompass various domains, including fine motor control, balance, and overall cognitive function. Early intervention programs targeting neurodevelopmental therapy and behavioral support are critical components of care.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits intermittent ear infections and difficulty tolerating loud noises, indicative of sensorineural hearing loss and otitis media.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Sensorineural hearing loss is a hallmark of KBG syndrome, affecting approximately 20-40% of individuals. Audiological evaluations and consideration of hearing aids or cochlear implants are recommended for managing auditory deficits.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient faces ocular concerns such as astigmatism, short-sightedness (myopia), and possible strabismus, impacting visual acuity and binocular vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Ocular anomalies are prevalent in KBG syndrome, including refractive errors, strabismus, and potentially optic nerve hypoplasia. Regular ophthalmologic examinations and appropriate corrective lenses or therapies are vital for maintaining optimal visual function.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient displays skin characteristics such as eczema-like patches and hyperpigmentation, which are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skin manifestations in KBG syndrome include eczema, vitiligo, and café-au-lait spots, among others. Dermatological management focuses on symptomatic relief and adherence to skincare routines.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity, particularly with exposure to cold temperatures, reflecting enamel vulnerability and potential dental caries.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental issues are frequent in KBG syndrome, involving weak enamel, susceptibility to cavities, and orthodontic considerations for malocclusion correction. Frequent dental check-ups and personalized treatment plans are essential.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires additional educational support, including accommodations for learning disabilities and behavioral differences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educational outcomes in KBG syndrome vary widely, with some achieving mainstream success while others require specialized environments. Individualized education plans (IEPs) and targeted therapeutic approaches are crucial for maximizing academic achievement.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety, which impact social interactions and routine behaviors.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioral profiles in KBG syndrome encompass a range of traits, including ASD, ADHD, and anxiety disorders. Therapeutic interventions, including behavior modification techniques and psychosocial support, play pivotal roles in shaping adaptive coping mechanisms.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient presents with skeletal anomalies such as brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth finger), contributing to a unique limb profile.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal features in KBG syndrome include brachydactyly, short fingers, and a distinctive hand morphology. Orthopedic evaluation and consideration of corrective surgeries are advisable for enhancing functional capabilities.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Vaccinations: Continue to administer vaccines against pneumococcus and Haemophilus influenzae type b to prevent respiratory tract infections.
b) Heart Monitoring: Maintain regular follow-up appointments for echocardiograms and ECGs to monitor valve function and detect any progression of heart-related issues.
c) Hearing Evaluation: Schedule audiometric checks every year starting from age two to assess hearing thresholds and rule out conductive hearing loss.
d) Vision Screening: Conduct comprehensive eye exams annually to identify and address ocular concerns such as astigmatism and myopia.
e) Undescended Testes: Monitor the position of testes in boys and consider surgical intervention if necessary.
f) Dental Care: Implement a rigorous dental hygiene regimen and schedule biannual dental check-ups to prevent tooth decay and maintain oral health.
g) Cardiac Surveillance: Follow the prescribed cardiac screening protocol post-diagnosis to track valve function and address any emerging heart conditions.
h) Tethered Cord Review: Evaluate for tethered cord syndrome through MRI imaging if clinical suspicion arises.
i) Palate Assessment: Refer for specialist review if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns.
j) Growth Monitoring: Keep a vigilant eye on height percentile and initiate endocrine investigations if height falls outside the 2nd centile.
k) Physiotherapy: Engage in regular physiotherapy sessions to improve coordination and reduce the risk of falls.
l) Occupational Therapy: Utilize occupational therapy to enhance fine motor skills and daily living abilities.
m) Speech Therapy: Collaborate with speech therapists to address feeding difficulties, speech delay, and potential swallowing concerns.
n) Behavioural Therapy: Incorporate behavior modification techniques and psychological counseling to manage behavioral challenges.
o) Dietary Modifications: Tailor dietary recommendations based on specific nutritional deficiencies and digestive sensitivities.
p) Nutritional Support: Ensure adequate intake of vitamins and minerals through supplementation or fortified diets.
q) Epilepsy Management: Monitor seizure activity and adjust antiepileptic drug regimens as necessary.
r) Thyroid Function Testing: Consider thyroid function testing in children with suspected hormonal imbalances.
s) Vitamin D Supplementation: Administer vitamin D supplements to mitigate the effects of reduced sunlight exposure and impaired calcium absorption.
t) Bone Density Assessments: Perform X-rays of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull to evaluate bone density and rule out osteoporosis.
u) Sleep Hygiene: Establish a consistent sleep schedule and promote relaxation techniques to optimize sleep patterns.
v) Regular Medical Reviews: Attend annual pediatrician consultations to address any emergent health concerns promptly.
w) Genetic Counseling: Offer genetic counseling services to provide emotional support and guidance for families considering future pregnancies.
x) Psychological Support: Provide access to mental health resources and counseling for caregivers and the patient themselves.
y) Family Planning: Discuss fertility options with geneticists and reproductive experts to explore viable alternatives for couples planning a family.

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child frequently experiences respiratory infections, requiring hospitalization and prolonged stays due to complications like pneumonia and bronchiolitis. These episodes lead to extended periods of rest and decreased activity levels.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Respiratory infections are frequent and can be severe in individuals with KBG syndrome, leading to hospitalizations and prolonged recovery times.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child requires regular cardiovascular monitoring due to a septal defect, which necessitates ongoing medical care and potential interventions like pacemaker placement.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Individuals with KBG syndrome commonly have congenital heart defects, including septal defects, which require lifelong medical supervision and potential surgical intervention.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child exhibits feeding difficulties, characterized by poor appetite and challenges with swallowing and chewing. These issues contribute to nutritional deficiencies and delayed growth.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Feeding difficulties are a hallmark of KBG syndrome, impacting the nutritional status and growth trajectory of affected individuals.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child faces immunodeficiency-related health risks, including susceptibility to infections and autoimmune reactions. Frequent vaccinations have been postponed due to these vulnerabilities.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Immunodeficiencies are a common feature in KBG syndrome, increasing the risk of infections and autoimmune disorders.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child displays neurodevelopmental delays, characterized by slower cognitive and motor skill acquisition compared to peers without the condition. Behavioral differences are also noted.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Neurodevelopmental delays and behavioral differences are consistent findings in KBG syndrome, affecting various aspects of cognition, behavior, and social interaction.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child suffers from persistent otitis media and hearing loss, necessitating regular ENT consultations and consideration of hearing aid usage.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Persistent ear infections and hearing loss are recurring issues in KBG syndrome, impacting communication and academic performance.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child exhibits ocular anomalies, including shallow anterior fontanelles and possible strabismus, which impact visual acuity and binocular vision.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Ocular anomalies are frequently observed in KBG syndrome, influencing visual outcomes and potentially affecting depth perception and coordination.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child presents with distinctive facial features, including synophrys (joined eyebrows), wide-set eyes, and a triangular-shaped face, which are hallmarks of KBG syndrome.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Distinctive facial features are a defining characteristic of KBG syndrome, contributing to its diagnostic criteria.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child experiences tooth sensitivity and frequent dental issues, necessitating meticulous oral hygiene practices and regular dental appointments.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Tooth sensitivity and frequent dental problems are common among individuals with KBG syndrome, highlighting the importance of comprehensive oral care.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child benefits from specialized educational programs tailored to address his unique learning needs, including additional support and accommodations.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Specialized educational approaches are crucial for managing the diverse learning requirements faced by individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child demonstrates behavioral differences, including autistic-like traits and attention deficits, which impact his interactions and adaptability.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Behavioral differences are a core component of KBG syndrome, influencing social behaviors, emotional regulation, and adaptive abilities.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child exhibits skeletal anomalies, including brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth finger), which influence his physical development and posture.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Skeletal abnormalities are a hallmark of KBG syndrome, impacting musculoskeletal health and gait patterns.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Regular dental check-ups: To maintain oral health and prevent tooth decay and gum disease.
b) Regular hearing reviews: To monitor auditory function and address any hearing impairments promptly.
c) Ophthalmology review: To assess vision and detect any ocular anomalies early.
d) Cardiac review: To monitor for heart conditions and ensure timely interventions.
e) Skeletal review: To evaluate bone age, hip, spine, and skull structures for any structural anomalies.
f) Palate review: To address feeding difficulties and speech development.
g) Consider a tethered cord review: Given the prevalence of this condition in KBG syndrome, it is advisable to investigate for tethered cord in infants with suspected anomalies.
h) Growth monitoring: To track height and weight trajectories and intervene if necessary.
i) Physiotherapy: To promote optimal physical development and reduce the risk of musculoskeletal issues.
j) Occupational therapy: To enhance functional abilities and improve daily living skills.
k) Speech therapy: To support language development and facilitate effective communication.
l) Behavioural therapy: To address behavioral differences and develop coping strategies.
m) Vaccination schedule: To protect against infectious diseases while minimizing adverse effects.
n) Medical review for cranial nerve involvement: To rule out issues related to the brainstem and peripheral nerves.
o) Genetic counseling: To provide families with information and support regarding the condition and future possibilities.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences occasional respiratory infections and requires vaccinations against pneumococcus and Haemophilus influenzae type b.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Respiratory infections are common in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the presence of functional ANKRD11 variants or deletions.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a history of transient ischemic attacks (TIAs) and seizures, which are consistent with the cardiovascular system being involved in KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Cardiovascular involvement, including TIAs and seizures, is commonly observed in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the functional ANKRD11 variants or deletions.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties and occasional vomiting, which are consistent with gastrointestinal concerns associated with KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and occasional vomiting are frequent complications in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the ANKRD11 gene mutation.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a history of seizures requiring medication adjustments, indicating ongoing immunological challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Seizure management and immunological challenges are common in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the functional ANKRD11 variants or deletions.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a history of epilepsy, which is consistent with neurological concerns observed in KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Epilepsy is a frequent neurological complication in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the ANKRD11 gene mutation.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences hearing concerns, including recurrent otitis media and hearing aid use, which are consistent with ENT issues observed in KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Hearing concerns, including recurrent otitis media and hearing aid use, are frequent in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the ANKRD11 gene mutation.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced vision concerns, including astigmatism and short-sightedness (myopia), which are consistent with ophthalmologic issues observed in KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision concerns, including astigmatism and short-sightedness (myopia), are frequent in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the ANKRD11 gene mutation.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced skin concerns, including eczema-like patches, which are consistent with dermatologic issues observed in KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skin concerns, including eczema-like patches, are frequent in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the ANKRD11 gene mutation.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires more frequent dental visits and uses braces, which are consistent with dental concerns observed in KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns, including more frequent dental visits and the need for braces, are frequent in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the ANKRD11 gene mutation.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient attends a mainstream primary school but requires additional support and accommodations, reflecting the educational challenges faced by individuals with KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educational challenges, including needing additional support and accommodations, are common in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the ANKRD11 gene mutation.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD) traits, which are consistent with the behavioral concerns observed in KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioral differences, including ASD traits, are frequent in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the ANKRD11 gene mutation.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increase in curvature of the spine (scoliosis), which is consistent with skeletal concerns observed in KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal concerns, including an unusual structure of the spinal bones leading to an increase in curvature of the spine (scoliosis), are frequent in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the ANKRD11 gene mutation.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
- Regular dental check-ups.
- Regular hearing reviews to age 5 (even if earlier reviews give a clear response).
- Ophthalmology review.
- Consider a palate review (particularly if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns).
- Referral for a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) following diagnosis.
- If nothing is found (or already done) this does not need to be repeated.
- Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist (to determine bone age), hip, spine and skull) in children following diagnosis.
- Any concerns around asymmetric hip creases in infancy and/or asymmetric or painful gait should prompt medical review.
- Consider review and investigation for tethered cord (MRI) where clinical concerns arise on an individual basis (especially if sacral dimple is present).
- Monitor growth velocity: if height is below the 2nd centile consider referral for endocrine investigations on an individual basis and within context of familial heights.
- Work closely with neurologists to adjust medications and recognize signs of upcoming seizures.
- Continue managing seizures with prescribed antiepileptic drugs as per current treatment plan.
- Maintain close communication with pediatricians and specialists regarding the patient's overall health and progress.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent respiratory infections
- Occasional asthma-like symptoms
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Variable susceptibility to respiratory infections
- Potential for developing asthma

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- Heart murmurs noted on echocardiogram
- Monitoring for potential arrhythmias
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Common occurrence of congenital heart defects
- Increased risk of arrhythmias

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent gastrointestinal infections
- Possible delayed gastric emptying
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Susceptibility to gastrointestinal infections
- Potential for delayed gastric emptying

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- Need for regular vaccinations
- Increased susceptibility to viral illnesses
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Higher likelihood of vaccine reactions
- Increased susceptibility to viral illnesses

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- Episodes of staring spells
- Impaired balance and coordination
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Common occurrence of similar neurological features

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
- Persistent nasal congestion
- Otitis media requiring frequent antibiotic treatments
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Susceptibility to otitis media

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
- Presbyopia (delayed onset of farsightedness)
- Astigmatism requiring corrective lenses
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Delayed onset of presbyopia

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- Hyperpigmentation of the skin
- Fine hair distribution
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Common occurrence of similar dermatological features

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent dental visits for fillings and extractions
- Specific dietary restrictions based on tooth sensitivity
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Susceptibility to dental issues

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
- Requires additional educational support
- May struggle with social interactions
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Likely to benefit from specialized educational programs

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
- Displays characteristics of autism spectrum disorder (ASD)
- Challenges with executive functions
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Consistent presence of ASD traits

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
- Presence of brachydactyly (short fingers)
- Curvature of the fifth finger (clinodactyly)
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Common occurrence of similar skeletal features

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
- Regular dental check-ups
- Monitoring for potential cardiovascular issues
- Management of gastrointestinal infections
- Vaccination schedule tailored to individual needs
- Speech therapy evaluations
- Occupational therapy assessments
- Behavioral therapy interventions
- Nutritional counseling for food texture preferences
- Orthodontic evaluation for possible treatment
- Follow-up cranial MRI for tethered cord concerns
- Genetic counseling for family members
- Regular physical examinations for early detection of health issues

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child experiences occasional respiratory infections, primarily viral in nature, which resolve without complications. He has a history of recurrent otitis media requiring multiple grommet insertions and occasional episodes of glue ear, affecting his hearing acuity.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Approximately 15%-38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve abnormalities, atrial septal defects, and patent ductus arteriosus. These conditions can lead to various cardiovascular issues, including arrhythmias, pulmonary hypertension, and heart failure.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child has experienced two instances of ventricular septal defect repair surgeries. Post-surgery, he continues to require echocardiograms and follow-up appointments with pediatric cardiologists to monitor his heart health and ensure proper healing.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Heart conditions are relatively common in individuals with KBG syndrome, with approximately 15%-38% experiencing congenital heart defects. These conditions can vary in severity and may require surgical interventions, lifelong medication, and regular follow-up care.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child has exhibited feeding aversion, particularly concerning certain textures and flavors. This has led to challenges in achieving adequate nutrition and potentially impacting his overall growth and development.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Individuals with KBG syndrome commonly encounter gastrointestinal issues, including reflux, constipation, and food intolerances. These conditions can contribute to nutritional deficiencies and delayed growth, highlighting the importance of dietary management and close monitoring.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child has shown sensitivity to vaccinations, necessitating additional doses or alternative immunizations to achieve sufficient immunity against common illnesses.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Vaccination reactions are not uncommon in individuals with KBG syndrome, as the immune system may be compromised. Additional doses or alternative vaccines are often recommended to provide comprehensive protection against infectious diseases.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child displays subtle behavioral differences, including heightened sensory sensitivities and social communication delays. Neurological evaluations have highlighted variations in brain structure and function, warranting ongoing neuropsychological assessments.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Behavioral differences are frequent in individuals with KBG syndrome, characterized by autism spectrum traits, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety. Neuropsychological testing helps identify specific areas of concern and guides targeted interventions.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child has experienced recurrent otitis media, necessitating multiple grommet insertions and occasional episodes of glue ear. These conditions can affect his hearing acuity and quality of life.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Ear, nose, and throat issues are prevalent in KBG syndrome, contributing to hearing loss and speech delays. Regular ENT consultations and monitoring are crucial to address these concerns effectively.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child has been diagnosed with astigmatism, affecting his ability to focus on distant objects. Regular eye examinations and corrective lenses are essential to maintain optimal visual clarity.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Vision problems are a hallmark of KBG syndrome, with studies reporting high rates of refractive errors and ocular anomalies. Ophthalmologic evaluations are vital for timely intervention and management.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child shows no dermatological concerns beyond the typical skin texture noted in individuals with KBG syndrome.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
No specific dermatological concerns were mentioned in the clinical reference guidelines, suggesting that this area is generally well-managed in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child faces challenges with tooth durability, requiring meticulous oral hygiene practices and frequent dental visits. Periodic X-rays and orthodontic evaluations are necessary to address potential skeletal anomalies and prevent future dental issues.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Dental concerns are common among individuals with KBG syndrome, including weak enamel, susceptibility to cavities, and bruxism. Close supervision and proactive dental care are essential to safeguard oral health.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child benefits from specialized educational programs tailored to his unique needs. While many attend mainstream primary schools, some require additional support in secondary settings. His academic progress reflects his strengths in subjects like art and music, while areas like mathematics and reading show room for improvement.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Education outcomes for individuals with KBG syndrome vary widely. Many thrive in inclusive environments with adapted curricula and supports, whereas others require more intensive interventions in specialized settings. Continuous evaluation and adjustment of educational strategies are critical for maximizing potential.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child exhibits characteristics consistent with the behavioral profile associated with KBG syndrome, including heightened sensory sensitivities, social communication delays, and occasional regression in developmental milestones.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Behavioral profiles in individuals with KBG syndrome encompass a range of traits, including autism spectrum behaviors, ADHD, and anxiety. Tailored therapeutic approaches, including behavior therapy, speech therapy, and occupational therapy, are integral components of managing these complexities.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child presents with skeletal anomalies, including brachydactyly and clinodactyly, which influence his physical capabilities and gait. Monitoring his skeletal development through X-rays and considering orthopedic referrals is essential.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Skeletal anomalies are frequent in KBG syndrome, involving irregular bone structures and joint flexibility issues. Regular skeletal assessments and consideration of orthopedic input are crucial for ensuring optimal functional outcomes.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Regular dental check-ups: To monitor and address dental issues promptly.
b) Regular hearing reviews: To ensure hearing thresholds are within normal limits.
c) Eye checks: To track vision progression and intervene early if necessary.
d) Cardiac follow-up: To monitor for any persistent heart conditions and address them appropriately.
e) Orthopedic assessment: To evaluate skeletal development and consider necessary interventions.
f) Behavioral therapy: To address sensory sensitivities and social communication deficits.
g) Speech therapy: To aid in improving speech and language abilities.
h) Occupational therapy: To enhance fine motor skills and daily living activities.
i) Physical therapy: To support mobility and reduce the risk of falls.
j) Epilepsy management: Given the prevalence of seizures in KBG syndrome, ongoing seizure management and review are essential.
k) Growth hormone therapy: Although not universally indicated, discussion with a specialist regarding its potential benefits is advised.
l) Vestibular rehabilitation: To assist with balance and coordination, especially beneficial for those with sensorineural hearing loss.
m) Gluten-free, lactose-free diet: Considering for suspected gluten-related disorders.
n) Vitamin D supplementation: Given the higher incidence of vitamin D deficiency in KBG syndrome, routine supplementation may be considered.
o) Thyroid function tests: To rule out hypothyroidism, which can manifest differently in individuals with KBG syndrome.
p) Endocrine screening: Including TSH, T4, and ACTH levels, depending on clinical presentation and family history.
q) Genetic counseling: For families considering future pregnancies, given the hereditary nature of the condition.
r) Psychological support: For caregivers and siblings, addressing emotional and psychological impacts of the diagnosis.
s) Family planning considerations: Discussing options for fertility preservation and genetic counseling for future pregnancies.
t) Long-term follow-up: Ensuring continued monitoring and management of newly identified medical concerns.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient complains of blurred vision and difficulty understanding speech.
- Blurred vision and difficulty understanding speech are noted.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome commonly complain of blurred vision and difficulty understanding speech.
- Difficulty comprehending speech is a frequent concern in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has a valve issue affecting his heart.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Valve issues are a common finding in individuals with KBG syndrome.
- Heart valve abnormalities are among the most frequently reported cardiovascular features in KBG syndrome.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient is described as being very picky with food textures, refusing certain foods due to texture concerns.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome often exhibit selective eating behaviors, avoiding certain textures or flavors.
- Selective eating is a recognized feature in KBG syndrome, impacting dietary preferences and intake.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has epilepsy, characterized by seizures.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Epilepsy is a common neurological feature in individuals with KBG syndrome.
- Seizure activity is frequently observed in those with KBG syndrome.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient experiences difficulty hearing, particularly with background noise.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Hearing difficulties are a recurring issue in KBG syndrome, exacerbated by background noise.
- Challenges with auditory processing and comprehension are common among individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has difficulty understanding speech, potentially due to visual processing challenges.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Visual processing difficulties are a known aspect of KBG syndrome, impacting communication abilities.
- Speech comprehension issues are frequently associated with visual processing challenges in KBG syndrome.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient exhibits selective eating behavior, specifically regarding food textures.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Selective eating is a hallmark of KBG syndrome, influencing dietary choices and overall nutrition.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient requires additional help in school due to speech delays and selective eating habits.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome typically require supplementary educational support, often necessitating Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) or Special Educational Needs Statements (SEN statements).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient displays behavioral differences, possibly related to autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioral differences are a consistent observation in KBG syndrome, contributing to social and emotional challenges.
- Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) are frequently reported comorbidities in KBG syndrome.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, leading to potential scoliosis.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Spinal deformities, such as scoliosis, are relatively common in individuals with KBG syndrome.
- Skeletal anomalies, including spinal curvature, are frequently encountered in KBG syndrome.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
- **Vision:** Regular eye examinations to address potential vision impairments and ensure proper refractive correction.
- **Hearing:** Ongoing audiometric evaluations to monitor hearing thresholds and address any hearing loss.
- **Speech Therapy:** Continued speech therapy sessions to enhance articulation, improve vocal quality, and facilitate better communication.
- **Orthodontics:** Periodic orthodontic assessments to address potential dental issues and correct malocclusions.
- **Cardiology:** Regular echocardiograms and ECGs to monitor cardiac health and detect any underlying heart conditions.
- **Neurological Management:** Ongoing seizure management with appropriate anticonvulsant medications and close monitoring.
- **Nutrition:** Encouraging a balanced diet rich in vitamins and minerals to support overall health and cognitive development.
- **Behavioral Support:** Implementing targeted behavioral interventions to address ASD-related behaviors and promote social interaction.
- **Physical Therapy:** Engaging in physical therapy programs to maintain muscle strength, flexibility, and coordination.
- **Monitoring Growth:** Continuous monitoring of height and weight to track growth velocity and identify any concerning trends.
- **Referral for Review:** Considering referrals for specialized craniofacial consultations and palate evaluation for children with suspected anomalies.
- **Vaccinations:** Ensuring timely vaccinations according to recommended schedules, while considering individual risk factors and healthcare provider recommendations.
- **Endocrine Evaluation:** Conducting periodic endocrine panel testing to rule out hormonal imbalances and provide appropriate treatment if necessary.
- **Psychological Assessment:** Offering psychological assessments and counseling services to support mental health and emotional well-being.
- **Support Groups and Resources:** Connecting families with local support groups and online communities to share experiences and receive valuable guidance.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child experiences occasional respiratory infections, particularly colds and flu-like illnesses, which can lead to coughing and difficulty breathing. These episodes are manageable with over-the-counter medications and rest.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Respiratory infections are relatively common in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the presence of a weakened immune system. While most children with KBG syndrome do not develop severe respiratory complications, managing frequent infections remains crucial for overall health and preventing hospitalizations.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child requires regular cardiovascular assessments due to the potential for heart-related issues. Monitoring includes echocardiograms and ECGs to ensure there are no structural abnormalities or arrhythmias.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Heart conditions are a common concern in KBG syndrome. The risk increases with the size of the ANKRD11 deletion or variant. Regular cardiovascular evaluations are essential to detect and manage any underlying heart defects promptly.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child exhibits digestive issues, characterized by frequent gastrointestinal infections and occasional constipation. Dietary adjustments and probiotics have helped improve his digestion.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Digestive disturbances are frequent in KBG syndrome. Children with larger ANKRD11 deletions or variants may experience more pronounced gastrointestinal symptoms. Managing dietary triggers and maintaining gut health is critical.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child faces challenges with vaccine responses due to compromised immunity. Frequent booster shots and close monitoring are necessary to prevent infectious diseases.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Vaccine reactions are heightened in individuals with KBG syndrome due to their weaker immune systems. Close surveillance and timely administration of vaccines are vital to protect against contagious illnesses.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child displays behavioral differences, including attention deficit and hyperactivity. Behavioral interventions and supportive therapies have shown positive results in improving his social interactions and focus.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Behavioral characteristics are commonly associated with KBG syndrome. Addressing behavioral concerns through therapeutic approaches and providing a nurturing environment can significantly enhance quality of life.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child experiences temporary hearing loss following exposure to loud noise, requiring audiometric checks and possible hearing aid usage.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Temporary hearing impairments are not uncommon in KBG syndrome. Ensuring adequate ventilation and minimizing exposure to loud environments is key to preventing prolonged hearing issues.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child requires regular ophthalmological examinations due to the potential for vision problems like astigmatism and short-sightedness (myopia). Early intervention helps maintain optimal visual acuity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Vision concerns are prevalent in KBG syndrome. Ongoing eye care and addressing refractive errors promptly is essential for preserving visual function.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child has a tendency towards eczema flare-ups, exacerbated by irritants and stress. Gentle skincare routines and avoiding known triggers have helped manage his skin condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Atopic dermatitis (eczema) is a hallmark of KBG syndrome. Maintaining a gentle skincare routine and identifying and avoiding allergens are crucial for controlling symptoms.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child requires more frequent dental visits compared to his peers due to the likelihood of developing cavities and gum issues. Professional cleanings and fluoride treatments are recommended.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Dental problems are frequent in KBG syndrome. Preventative measures such as regular dental check-ups and proper oral hygiene practices are essential for maintaining oral health.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child benefits from additional educational support, including one-to-one tutoring and specialized programs tailored to his unique needs. Progress in mainstream schools has been mixed, with some excelling while others require more intensive interventions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Educational outcomes vary widely among individuals with KBG syndrome. Providing targeted support, accommodations, and resources specifically designed for the syndrome can significantly impact academic achievement and social integration.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child demonstrates behavioral traits consistent with KBG syndrome, including sensitivity to stimuli and occasional temper tantrums. Therapeutic interventions aimed at emotional regulation and behavior modification have proven beneficial.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Behavioral manifestations are typical in KBG syndrome. Implementing therapeutic strategies focused on emotional intelligence and behavioral management can greatly alleviate distress and promote healthier coping mechanisms.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child experiences brachydactyly, characterized by shortened fingers, and clinodactyly, resulting in inward-curving of the fifth finger. Orthodontic treatment and splints have helped mitigate physical limitations.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Bone structure anomalies are common in KBG syndrome. Addressing orthopedic concerns through braces, splints, and corrective surgeries can optimize functional capabilities and reduce pain.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Management of Respiratory Infections:
- Encourage frequent hand washing and avoidance of crowded places.
- Maintain a healthy immune system through balanced nutrition and regular exercise.
- Keep vaccinations up-to-date according to pediatricians' recommendations.

b) Cardiovascular Monitoring:
- Schedule regular echocardiograms and ECGs.
- Follow cardiologist guidance regarding medication and lifestyle modifications.

c) Vaccine Responses:
- Administer vaccines as per pediatricians' recommendations.
- Monitor for adverse reactions closely and seek medical attention immediately.

d) Digestive Issues:
- Adopt a balanced diet rich in fiber and vitamins.
- Incorporate probiotic supplements to support gut health.
- Avoid trigger foods and maintain a consistent feeding schedule.

e) Vision Concerns:
- Perform annual comprehensive eye exams.
- Use prescribed eyewear and adhere to eye care protocols.

f) Skin Conditions:
- Apply gentle, fragrance-free moisturizers.
- Identify and avoid allergens triggering eczema flare-ups.
- Consult dermatologists for advanced treatments and management plans.

g) Dental Care:
- Schedule biannual dental appointments.
- Implement a rigorous home-care regimen focusing on plaque control and oral hygiene.
- Consider sealant applications and fluoride treatments for added protection.

h) Educational Support:
- Engage with educational specialists and therapists.
- Explore options for homeschooling or specialized educational programs.
- Advocate for inclusive classroom environments and assistive technologies.

i) Behavioral Interventions:
- Utilize behavior therapy techniques to manage sensitivities and tantrums.
- Promote mindfulness and relaxation exercises to enhance emotional regulation.
- Collaborate with educators and caregivers to create a cohesive approach to behavior management.

j) Skeletal Management:
- Monitor bone density through X-rays and ultrasounds.
- Consider orthodontic consultations for potential jaw alignment issues.
- Evaluate eligibility for surgical interventions as advised by orthopedic experts.

k) Medical Screening:
- Conduct periodic thyroid function tests.
- Review kidney function periodically.
- Monitor hormonal profiles for any irregularities.
- Stay vigilant for early signs of autoimmune disorders.

l) Immunization Program:
- Adhere to immunization schedules recommended by pediatricians.
- Seek clarification on exceptions or alternative regimens if applicable.

m) Nutritional Guidance:
- Consult a registered dietician specializing in rare genetic conditions.
- Emphasize the importance of protein intake and vitamin supplementation.
- Tailor dietary recommendations based on individual nutritional needs.

n) Psychological Support:
- Offer counseling services for parents and siblings dealing with the syndrome.
- Participate in support groups for families navigating similar challenges.
- Foster open communication between parents, healthcare providers, and educators to address psychological needs comprehensively.

o) Long-Term Surveillance:
- Regularly revisit pediatricians and geneticists for updates.
- Stay informed about emerging research and best practices in treating KBG syndrome.
- Be prepared to adjust treatment plans and management strategies as new insights emerge."

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child experiences frequent respiratory infections, particularly colds and bronchitis. These infections tend to recur more frequently than in his peers without KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Respiratory infections are common in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the combination of anatomical and physiological factors associated with the condition.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child has experienced episodes of syncope (fainting) attributed to cardiovascular issues. These events were managed medically and resolved with treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Syncope is a potential complication in individuals with KBG syndrome due to underlying cardiovascular concerns, such as arrhythmias or structural heart defects.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child exhibits gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), characterized by regurgitation of food and acid back up into the esophagus. This leads to discomfort and occasional difficulty swallowing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
GERD is a recognized gastrointestinal issue in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the presence of functional gastrointestinal tract dysfunction.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child has demonstrated hypersensitivity reactions, specifically urticaria (hives) and angioedema (swelling beneath the skin). These allergic reactions can flare up unpredictably.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Allergic reactions are a known component of KBG syndrome due to the genetic variation affecting immune system regulation.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child displays behavioral differences, including attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and anxiety. These behaviors impact his social interactions and academic performance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Behavioral differences are commonly observed in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the neurodevelopmental aspects of the condition.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child suffers from chronic sinusitis, characterized by recurring nasal congestion and purulent discharge. This condition impacts his overall airway patency and sleep patterns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Chronic sinusitis is a frequent occurrence in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the anatomical and immunological alterations associated with the condition.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child has undergone corrective laser eye surgery to address his refractive errors, improving his visual acuity and reducing the risk of amblyopia (lazy eye).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Corrective surgeries for refractive errors are routine procedures in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the prevalence of myopia and astigmatism.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child presents with eczema, a common skin condition exacerbated by environmental triggers and irritants. Frequent flare-ups necessitate topical corticosteroids and moisturizers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Eczema is a prevalent dermatological issue in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the genetic predisposition towards immune-mediated inflammatory diseases.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child faces challenges with tooth eruption and dental hygiene, leading to early loss of baby teeth and delayed permanent tooth development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Early tooth loss and delayed permanent tooth development are typical observations in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the genetic variations impacting craniofacial and skeletal development.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child attends a mainstream primary school but requires additional educational support to meet his cognitive and behavioral needs. Transition to secondary school remains challenging given his behavioral profile.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Transition to secondary school is often fraught with difficulties for individuals with KBG syndrome due to the cumulative effects of developmental delays, behavioral differences, and sensory sensitivities.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child demonstrates characteristics consistent with the behavioral phenotype of KBG syndrome, including executive function deficits, anxiety, and mood swings.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Executive function deficits and behavioral differences are hallmarks of KBG syndrome due to the neurodevelopmental impairments inherent to the condition.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child exhibits brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth finger), contributing to his unique hand morphology.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Brachydactyly and clinodactyly are observed in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the genetic variations affecting bone development and cartilage formation.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Seizures:
Continue current antiepileptic medications as per pediatric neurologists' recommendations. Monitor seizure frequency and adjust dosages accordingly.
b) Hearing:
Maintain regular audiometric evaluations every 6 months post-diagnosis. Address any persistent hearing concerns promptly.
c) Vision:
Prescribe appropriate topical corticosteroids and recommend regular follow-up appointments with an ophthalmologist.
d) Heart:
Monitor for signs of worsening heart conditions. Follow cardiologists' recommendations regarding echocardiograms and ECGs.
e) Tethered Cord:
Consider MRI scans for infants with suspected tethered cord syndrome. Evaluate for sacral dimple and assess for positional trends.
f) Palate:
Refer for specialist review if there are ongoing feeding difficulties or speech concerns. Monitor for changes in feeding habits and speech milestones.
g) Dental:
Continue orthodontic monitoring and provide guidance on dietary modifications to promote healthy tooth development.
h) GI:
Review dietary restrictions and consult with a nutritionist for personalized meal plans. Implement strategies to reduce bowel irritants.
i) Behavioral:
Provide targeted behavior therapy sessions and implement routines to minimize stressors. Encourage parental involvement in therapeutic interventions.
j) Growth:
Monitor height percentile regularly. Consider referral for growth hormone therapy if height continues to fall below the 2nd centile.
k) Immunizations:
Ensure adherence to recommended vaccinations schedule. Discuss the necessity of additional prophylactic measures based on clinical assessment.
l) Orthopedics:
Follow orthopedic specialists for evaluation of skeletal anomalies. Consider surgical intervention for severe brachydactyly or other deformities.
m) Neurology:
Continue neuropsychological assessments and behavioral therapy programs. Review prescription of psychotropic medications periodically.
n) Endocrinology:
Conduct periodic thyroid function tests and evaluate for other hormonal imbalances. Refer for further investigation if concerns persist.
o) Cardiology:
Continue annual echocardiograms and ECGs. Consider referral for cardiac MRI if existing imaging fails to resolve concerns.
p) Ophthalmology:
Schedule comprehensive eye exams annually. Address any new onset vision issues promptly.
q) Dentistry:
Implement a detailed dental care plan tailored to our child's specific needs. Schedule biannual dental visits.
r) Speech Therapy:
Engage in speech therapy sessions focusing on articulation, volume control, and pragmatic communication skills. Monitor progress regularly.
s) Occupational Therapy:
Introduce specialized OT programs targeting fine motor skills, self-care abilities, and organizational techniques. Monitor improvements over time.
t) Physical Therapy:
Initiate a structured PT program emphasizing strength training, flexibility exercises, and balance activities. Monitor progression and make adjustments as necessary.
u) Behavioural Management:
Develop a structured behavioral management plan incorporating positive reinforcement techniques. Educate caregivers on effective discipline methods.
v) Parent Support Groups:
Encourage participation in local support groups for families dealing with similar conditions. Connect with online communities for additional resources and emotional support.
w) Genetic Counseling:
Advise family members considering pregnancy to undergo genetic counseling and testing. Discuss options for carrier screening and prenatal diagnostic testing.
x) Long-Term Monitoring:
Establish a multidisciplinary team consisting of pediatricians, neurologists, ENT specialists, dentists, speech therapists, occupational therapists, and psychologists. Maintain regular follow-up appointments to track progress and address emerging concerns.
y) Research Participation:
Inquire about opportunities for clinical trials or observational studies involving KBG syndrome. Stay informed about advancements in treatment and management approaches.
z) Family Planning:
Discuss considerations for future pregnancies with genetic counselors and discuss options for preimplantation genetic diagnosis (PGD) if applicable.
AA) Additional Recommendations:
Given the complexity of managing KBG syndrome, it is crucial to maintain open lines of communication between healthcare providers and the entire family. Regular updates and reassessments are essential to adapt treatment plans and address evolving needs. Additionally, fostering a supportive and inclusive environment within the family unit can greatly enhance the overall well-being and quality of life for individuals with KBG syndrome and their loved ones.
